KJ our Racer

By: Floris Kotze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Not your average teenager, this boy is a star in the making....

Unique Selling Point:
Passion driving young motorcycle rider (15) to glory

Lewis Hamilton admitted his dream as a child of one day making it into Formula 1 was ‘madness’. In a 2020 interview with Italian magazine Style, Hamilton said he was, however, lucky because his father pushed him not to give up.

These sentiments bring a smile to the face of Adrian Scholtz, CEO of Motorsport South Africa, because they currently have a rookie motorcycle rider under their wing with a very similar story – and hunger to succeed.

Scholtz says Kgopotso Mononyane ‘the second’ (affectionately known as KJ) is a 15-year-old from Johannesburg who eats, sleeps and breathes motorcycle racing.

Summary:
KJ, a Grade Nine learner at Waterstone College, recalls his first “break” came in 2017 (he was 10 years old) when Neil Harran from the South African Motorcycle Racing Academy visited his school’s open day.

“I was so excited to try out the demo stationary practice bike he had at the open day and everyone was very impressed with my test ride. Neil then recommended to my parents that I enrol into his academy. I was ecstatic as I knew this could be the start of great things to come,” KJ said.

And it was. KJ started participating competitively in the short circuit road racing series in 2017 (he was 10 years old) in the NSF100cc Honda Cup and won a championship in 2019.

In 2020, KJ claimed another title in the Clubman’s championship and finished second in the 150 cup – a category he went on to win the next year. He started competing in Italy in June 2021, in the middle of the racing season. To date, he has won multiple circuit motorcycle racing championships.

Further information:
Treatment Overview

Opening Scene and setup: 120 seconds
I would like to start the insert with a scene of the Mononyane family, getting ready for supper. A mother is dishing up, kids around the table. Happy talking, just normal…. Voice over is explaining that this might look like an “ordinary” family.
But they are far from it… We see KJ. We don’t know who he is, we are not sure what is about to happen….
We see KJ holding a spoon in his hand like a biker holds onto the throttle….
We are confused.
We see a close up of KJ’s face and we crash zoom to only his eyes.

Then a beautiful transition as we zoom out from a close up of his eyes at the table to a wider shot of him at the track. Pulling the helmet over his head or closing the visor….
We catch a glimpse of who he is. A bike racer.
We show a few highlights with breathtaking footage of him. Quick montage.
Then we cut back to him at the table.
We explain that this family is driven by his mother. There are 3 members in this family. Dad is absent…. We don’t explain why yet….
Mom is supporting her talented son on the bike. We hear how much sacrifice it takes. But how talented is he really….?

Motorsport SA and KJ as a person: 120 Seconds
Motorsport SA’s CEO Anton Roux explains exactly how talented KJ is… It is quite astounding. He has many many wins and countless podiums on the SA circuit, and then we hear how he raced overseas! Motorsport SA supported him to be able to race in Italy. And he did well, very well, he finished in the top 10.
We cut back to KJ holding a bunch of trophies, he is trying to explain which he won where, there are just too many, he forgets some of the races he won… So many podiums too.
Mom is telling us what a sacrifice it has been. But she has supported him all the way.
A Quick Montage of him racing and podiums, some amateur footage that the family shot, we show a very young KJ, 10 years old on a bike and we progress to today.
We now understand how good he really is.

Loss of his father: 120 seconds
But now comes the shock. Out of the blue KJ says he gave up racing. When he lost his dad. We explain what happened to his dad. He was in a Netcare helicopter crash that took the lives of 5 emergency crews and the pilot. This happened last year in January. On a weekend when KJ was not only racing, but waited for his dad at the track. He never arrived.
https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2021-02-23-netcare-911-helicopter-broke-up-in-flight-preliminary-probe-finds/
We stay with the family as they explain the trauma of going through this tragedy. KJ decided he can’t give up. It is something he and his dad started and he has to give it a good shot. His dad races with him everytime he gets on the bike. We see a sign on his race suit that says as we see a closeup of his race suit, a caption says: RIP Papa.

KJ and the 2023 season and end: 120 Seconds
We hear from experts that encourages KJ to go for it. To try and win National champs. We hear about the financial burden on the family. It is clearly a very expensive sport. But he has bigger ambitions. He is destined to go race in Europe in 2023, but it is simply not possible, financially.
Mom speaks and gives us a bit more info of where KJ is finding himself and what the chances of racing in Europe would be.
Motorsport SA is very positive, but the reality is it is tough. It leads us into his first race for 2023 at Red Star. He is only 1 of dozens, contenders, how well will he do.

His first race of 2023: 120 Seconds
Chaos at the race, we see lots of people running around. Fixing bikes. Loud engine noises. And in the midst of this chaos we see a very calm KJ. We pick up that pressure just doesn’t get to him. We ask him how he thinks he will do, he smiles, hopefully on the podium…
Then
Green light!
We see the race, it's exhilarating. He comes past the camera at speed! A rush! He goes well, but it is chaotic, exciting music and action packed. We cut to the reaction of Mom, very nervous, she can’t watch!
We follow him and he finishes the race. As predicted, he did very well!

Details of the insert
I want to approach this as a mini doccie on KJ. To showcase this talent of ours. The audience will connect to this family right from the start. It is important to make the family relatable to others. Just because he is racing motorbikes, does not make him any different to others. But what will come across is the tragedy of losing their father and husband. And their journey through this awful event.
KJ will let us into his home, school, and racetrack. He will drive the narrative without coming across as arrogant. He is really down to earth and we will see a very talented, positive, driven kid.
I have spent a lot of time with the family, to build up trust. So that when we have cameras, it will be normal for them.


Extra Budget Items:
Mac will have to watch KJ race on Sunday yhe 11th of February

Anton ROUX

Script:



Early morning
VO: The sun has just risen over southern Jo’burg.
Gap
VO: A family, gathered for breakfast, is getting ready for the day.
As serene as the picture appears, this family lives life in the fast lane!
Quick montage racing…
Opening Link:
A motorsport track in the East Rand may seem like an unconventional place to find a rising star… but, as you’ll soon find out, on that track behind me, is a teenager with a bright future!
My name is Kgopotso Mononyane people know me as KJ Kgopotso Junior and I'm a motorcycle racer!
I am 15 years old, I was 10 years old at the time I started racing and I really loved it!
VO: KJ's journey with motorcycles began in his childhood, when his father took him to a track. His natural talent was immediately evident.
KJ
I’ve had a passion for it, so I wanted to pursue it even more and pursue my dreams of becoming a MotoGP rider.
When I get on the bike it gives me happiness its my happy place every time I go back I will try to perfect that corner again and again and that's what makes you a champion!
Mom:
There's this element of fear, it’s too dangerous, and I wasn't approving at first.
VO:
But KJ and his dad persisted and, eventually, his mom, Kgomotso Mononyane, relented...
Mom:
I couldn't say no because I couldn't say no, he love that you could see you was enjoying it.
LINK: He was not just enjoying it, but he was also winning races and this is only after a few months of racing.



KJ:
There's a lot of trophies, I'm not too sure about all of them. I don't even have a lot of space for them honestly, I even keep some in the storeroom.
VO: KJ’s success attracted international interest. At just 13, he signed a contract to race for a season in one of Europe’s racing meccas: Italy. THIS was his big break… and all thanks to his DAD.
KJ:
My dad said to me that this is an opportunity for me to really pursue my dream. We decided to sign the contract!
Anton:
To be signed up by an international team in Italy says enough the mere fact that has been signed up, means that internationally is recognised as somebody with talent.
VO:
Anton Roux is the Chairman of Motorsport South Africa. MSA is the governing body for the sport and responsible for organizing and regulating events and activities. They helped K.J. to race overseas.
Anton: What we are trying to do is at least supporting him with his international licence fees, as well as his insurance cover and we assisting him in that fashion.
Mom:
My husband he was so excited that his son is going to be riding overseas and yeah it was a dream come true for him
VO: But, their lives took a tragic turn just two days after signing the contract in January 2021.
PODCAST:
Netcare helicopter pilot and a four-man team of highly specialised doctors died when the helicopter they were travelling in crashed alongside the N3.
VO: The helicopter went down outside Bergville, in KZN. KJ's father, an anaesthetist, was on board.



Mom:
I couldn't believe it, I was like, we were talking to him just now, so I didn't understand it.


KJ:
I felt like I just lost everything that day, my heart broke into a million pieces, I can't imagine that day, I wouldn't wanna live it again. it really affected me and my career. I couldn't race, I couldn't get on a bike.
Mom:
I miss him a lot. He wanted the best for his family he worked hard for his family. He made sure that he provides for his family, that made me to say you know I can't let him down. I will continue living his Legacy and making sure to build on what he has left.
KJ: It really affected me and my Career and my mental health. But I went to counselling sessions, we’re back in the game again!
VO:
As his dad had always hoped, K.J. joined the Italian team a few months later - but, only for the second half of the season, due to his father’s passing.
KJ:
It was good. It was really tough for the first time cuz I didn't know what to expect. I got points every race and I got top 10 almost every race, so I feel like that was a big accomplishment for me and the family.
Themba:
Losing his dad was extremely difficult and honestly I can't really say I understood what he went through but I do understand how strong he had to be throughout it.
Themba Khumalo is a professional superbike racer and has been kj's coach since 2019.
Themba:
I’m going to try not to over hype him but I'm very proud of K.J. I now look after 10 kids that I coach formally and he was the first. As a youngster I always wanted to share the knowledge that I gained with other youngsters from black backgrounds that need my support and the knowledge just to smoothen the journey, it is not easy being a black youngster, you know, I paving the way in motorsport. My job is essentially to refine the talent, you know, it's to take the diamond in the rough and make it shine. So if I've got a hardworking child that is willing to learn which is like KJ, then I can turn that into success.
VO: In a few months, K.J. is set to return to Italy, this time he'll be competing in the much tougher Moto3 class.
Mac: Do you think he’ll be able to do well overseas and how much more support would he need for him to be able to get in and play at those levels?
Anton:
It's a difficult question to answer but I always think about the words of Gary Player who said say you know the the more I try the luckier I get, and I think that's the case with him. He is talented but but talent is also gonna need a significant amount of funding. lot of luck, so I think he has got the ability but we gotta make sure that we also promote him as an individual and that he understands very early on in his career what he needs to do to attract sponsors, and we need more role models like him for the younger kids in South Africa. So I think he's got a bright future but unfortunately, he is gonna need a lot of luck as well.
Link:
Motorcycle racing in South Africa is an expensive sport but even if you do win a race you don't receive any prize money you have to win the overall championship.
Mom:
It's quite an expensive I wasn't aware of the expenses no they didn't tell me what it's what it was going to cost they both bikes and you know they were fixing I didn't know the expensive only after his dad’s passing where I had to take over and that's when I saw the actual costs and I was like am I going to be able to keep up with this? I mean it's a lot of money, the travelling costs when you go to the races the entry is that you pay, I don't want to see myself paying for this, it should be self-funding.
Commentator
Welcome to the SA Short Circuit Series Round 1, here at Vereeniging cart Circuit…
VO: Last week, K.J took part in his first race of 2023. And there was no shortage of drama.
KJ
When I close my visor everything changes I have am a different KJ that you'd never imagine, I am like a hungry lion that always wants to survive and be on the top step.
VO:
K.J. showed grit and determination as he outclassed the field to take the win recovering from last place!
Mom:
I know what my husband would want from me, he would want me to be strong, he would want me to carry our children and to make sure that we give them the best future.
KJ:
My dad is always with me,I feel like he's always with me with the bike. When I am racing sometimes I think about him when I‘m in first alone.


Coach:
He has high ambitions even for himself, so I'd love to see him become a world champion one day!








Promo 1
It's not everyday that we get to witness a star-in-the-making we follow KJ Mononyane and the blazes a trail around the world!

Promo 2:








LINK: Watching a single mother, dedicated to support her son’s racing, is inspiring. Every race weekend is a struggle, not only financially, but logistically and mechanically too. KJ has to rely on those good people around him for help…

Track Link: I have been trackside for a while now, keeping a close eye on KJ… and trust me when I tell you, he is FAST!
Track link: Motorcycle racing in South Africa is an expensive sport. You have to supply everything yourself, from the motorcycle, travelling and petrol. But even if you win a race, you don’t receive any prize money. You have to win the overall championship to receive any kind of money.

School Link:
Between school and homework, KJ even makes time to do other sports. His favourite is taekwondo. It keeps his body weight down and keeps him fit. He has to spend a lot of hours training. He is happy to do this, knowing it will make him faster on the bike.

END LINK: The untimely death of Kgopotso, KJ’s dad's death, left a massive void in the family, KJ was about to give up racing. But from a young age his dad instilled in him, the spirit of racing. And as a father myself, one day when I am unable to be there for my kids, I’d only want them to be happy. And that’s exactly what KJ is, that boy is delighted underneath that helmet….



TEASER ONE
VO: It’s fast… often unpredictable and very competitive.
UPSOUND: …KJ one why he loves motor racing…
VO: Now fifteen year old championship winning KJ Mononyane looks to be South Africa’s next elite motor racer!

TEASER TWO
VO: At 15-years-old, KJ Mononyane juggles books, extra-murals and… competitive motor racing…
UPSOUND:
VO: Already a championship winning racer… KJ could be South Africa’s next great elite motor racer.

TEASER THREE
{NEWS audio about the plane crash… }
VO: It was a horrific accident that changed his life…
UPSOUND: … something about losing his dad..
VO: … Now this 15-year-old champion in waiting - elite motor cycle racer KJ - is racing in the memory of his biggest supporter…

TEASER FOUR
[VIZ… back tyre of motorcycle, engine noise, tyres squeal… then it races off into the distance..]
VO: This, is KJ Mononyane… fast… determined and a ruthless competitor on track…
UPSOUND:
VO: … But could this rookie be South Africa’s next elite motor racer?

TEASER FIVE
VO: Tough to break into and even tougher to succeed … motorcycle racing is one of the most competitive sports in the world.
UPSOUND:
VO: But could 15 year old rookie - KJ Mononyane - be South Africa’s next elite motorcycle champion?










Promo 11” (TRACK)
It is not everyday that we get to witness a star in the making… We follow young KJ Mononyane, as he blazes a trail around the world!
Promo 11” (TRACK)
A family was ripped apart by a tragedy. We hear how they turned catastrophe into an inspiring story of hope.

Promo 21” 1 (TRACK)
VO: We follow the fastest teenager on 2 wheels!
KJ:
I always try to perfect a corner again and again and that's what makes you a champion! Racing just gives me that happiness and it shows who I really am.
VO: Young KJ Mononyane is ready for the top step in bike racing, blink and you’ll miss him!

Promo 21” 2 (TRACK)
VO: A blisteringly fast bike racer from Joburg was destined for glory. But then tragedy struck…
KJ:
At first I went through depression and it really affected me. I couldn't get on a bike that I didn't feel comfortable getting on a bike.
VO: We find out why KJ Mononyane was ready to quit racing…

Promo 21” 3 (TRACK)
VO: A young Joburg teenager turned heads whilst racing in Italy…
KJ: To come fifth place and tenth place in the overall championship is a big accomplishment for South Africa and me.
VO: We discover what it takes to race bikes at the top level.

Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 13 December 2023 26 February 2023 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 26 February 2023 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: Early morning VO: The sun has just risen over southern Jo’burg. Gap VO: A family, gathered for breakfast, is getting ready for the day. As serene as the picture appears, this family lives life in the fast lane! Quick montage racing… Opening Link: A motorsport track in the East Rand may seem like an unconventional place to find a rising star… but, as you’ll soon find out, on that track behind me, is a teenager with a bright future! My name is Kgopotso Mononyane people know me as KJ Kgopotso Junior and I'm a motorcycle racer! I am 15 years old, I was 10 years old at the time I started racing and I really loved it! VO: KJ's journey with motorcycles began in his childhood, when his father took him to a track. His natural talent was immediately evident. KJ I’ve had a passion for it, so I wanted to pursue it even more and pursue my dreams of becoming a MotoGP rider. When I get on the bike it gives me happiness its my happy place every time I go back I will try to perfect that corner again and again and that's what makes you a champion! Mom: There's this element of fear, it’s too dangerous, and I wasn't approving at first. VO: But KJ and his dad persisted and, eventually, his mom, Kgomotso Mononyane, relented... Mom: I couldn't say no because I couldn't say no, he love that you could see you was enjoying it. LINK: He was not just enjoying it, but he was also winning races and this is only after a few months of racing. KJ: There's a lot of trophies, I'm not too sure about all of them. I don't even have a lot of space for them honestly, I even keep some in the storeroom. VO: KJ’s success attracted international interest. At just 13, he signed a contract to race for a season in one of Europe’s racing meccas: Italy. THIS was his big break… and all thanks to his DAD. KJ: My dad said to me that this is an opportunity for me to really pursue my dream. We decided to sign the contract! Anton: To be signed up by an international team in Italy says enough the mere fact that has been signed up, means that internationally is recognised as somebody with talent. VO: Anton Roux is the Chairman of Motorsport South Africa. MSA is the governing body for the sport and responsible for organizing and regulating events and activities. They helped K.J. to race overseas. Anton: What we are trying to do is at least supporting him with his international licence fees, as well as his insurance cover and we assisting him in that fashion. Mom: My husband he was so excited that his son is going to be riding overseas and yeah it was a dream come true for him VO: But, their lives took a tragic turn just two days after signing the contract in January 2021. PODCAST: Netcare helicopter pilot and a four-man team of highly specialised doctors died when the helicopter they were travelling in crashed alongside the N3. VO: The helicopter went down outside Bergville, in KZN. KJ's father, an anaesthetist, was on board. Mom: I couldn't believe it, I was like, we were talking to him just now, so I didn't understand it. KJ: I felt like I just lost everything that day, my heart broke into a million pieces, I can't imagine that day, I wouldn't wanna live it again. it really affected me and my career. I couldn't race, I couldn't get on a bike. Mom: I miss him a lot. He wanted the best for his family he worked hard for his family. He made sure that he provides for his family, that made me to say you know I can't let him down. I will continue living his Legacy and making sure to build on what he has left. KJ: It really affected me and my Career and my mental health. But I went to counselling sessions, we’re back in the game again! VO: As his dad had always hoped, K.J. joined the Italian team a few months later - but, only for the second half of the season, due to his father’s passing. KJ: It was good. It was really tough for the first time cuz I didn't know what to expect. I got points every race and I got top 10 almost every race, so I feel like that was a big accomplishment for me and the family. Themba: Losing his dad was extremely difficult and honestly I can't really say I understood what he went through but I do understand how strong he had to be throughout it. Themba Khumalo is a professional superbike racer and has been kj's coach since 2019. Themba: I’m going to try not to over hype him but I'm very proud of K.J. I now look after 10 kids that I coach formally and he was the first. As a youngster I always wanted to share the knowledge that I gained with other youngsters from black backgrounds that need my support and the knowledge just to smoothen the journey, it is not easy being a black youngster, you know, I paving the way in motorsport. My job is essentially to refine the talent, you know, it's to take the diamond in the rough and make it shine. So if I've got a hardworking child that is willing to learn which is like KJ, then I can turn that into success. VO: In a few months, K.J. is set to return to Italy, this time he'll be competing in the much tougher Moto3 class. Mac: Do you think he’ll be able to do well overseas and how much more support would he need for him to be able to get in and play at those levels? Anton: It's a difficult question to answer but I always think about the words of Gary Player who said say you know the the more I try the luckier I get, and I think that's the case with him. He is talented but but talent is also gonna need a significant amount of funding. lot of luck, so I think he has got the ability but we gotta make sure that we also promote him as an individual and that he understands very early on in his career what he needs to do to attract sponsors, and we need more role models like him for the younger kids in South Africa. So I think he's got a bright future but unfortunately, he is gonna need a lot of luck as well. Link: Motorcycle racing in South Africa is an expensive sport but even if you do win a race you don't receive any prize money you have to win the overall championship. Mom: It's quite an expensive I wasn't aware of the expenses no they didn't tell me what it's what it was going to cost they both bikes and you know they were fixing I didn't know the expensive only after his dad’s passing where I had to take over and that's when I saw the actual costs and I was like am I going to be able to keep up with this? I mean it's a lot of money, the travelling costs when you go to the races the entry is that you pay, I don't want to see myself paying for this, it should be self-funding. Commentator Welcome to the SA Short Circuit Series Round 1, here at Vereeniging cart Circuit… VO: Last week, K.J took part in his first race of 2023. And there was no shortage of drama. KJ When I close my visor everything changes I have am a different KJ that you'd never imagine, I am like a hungry lion that always wants to survive and be on the top step. VO: K.J. showed grit and determination as he outclassed the field to take the win recovering from last place! Mom: I know what my husband would want from me, he would want me to be strong, he would want me to carry our children and to make sure that we give them the best future. KJ: My dad is always with me,I feel like he's always with me with the bike. When I am racing sometimes I think about him when I‘m in first alone. Coach: He has high ambitions even for himself, so I'd love to see him become a world champion one day! Promo 1 It's not everyday that we get to witness a star-in-the-making we follow KJ Mononyane and the blazes a trail around the world! Promo 2: LINK: Watching a single mother, dedicated to support her son’s racing, is inspiring. Every race weekend is a struggle, not only financially, but logistically and mechanically too. KJ has to rely on those good people around him for help… Track Link: I have been trackside for a while now, keeping a close eye on KJ… and trust me when I tell you, he is FAST! Track link: Motorcycle racing in South Africa is an expensive sport. You have to supply everything yourself, from the motorcycle, travelling and petrol. But even if you win a race, you don’t receive any prize money. You have to win the overall championship to receive any kind of money. School Link: Between school and homework, KJ even makes time to do other sports. His favourite is taekwondo. It keeps his body weight down and keeps him fit. He has to spend a lot of hours training. He is happy to do this, knowing it will make him faster on the bike. END LINK: The untimely death of Kgopotso, KJ’s dad's death, left a massive void in the family, KJ was about to give up racing. But from a young age his dad instilled in him, the spirit of racing. And as a father myself, one day when I am unable to be there for my kids, I’d only want them to be happy. And that’s exactly what KJ is, that boy is delighted underneath that helmet…. TEASER ONE VO: It’s fast… often unpredictable and very competitive. metadata.Unique Selling Point: Passion driving young motorcycle rider (15) to glory Lewis Hamilton admitted his dream as a child of one day making it into Formula 1 was ‘madness’. In a 2020 interview with Italian magazine Style, Hamilton said he was, however, lucky because his father pushed him not to give up. These sentiments bring a smile to the face of Adrian Scholtz, CEO of Motorsport South Africa, because they currently have a rookie motorcycle rider under their wing with a very similar story – and hunger to succeed. Scholtz says Kgopotso Mononyane ‘the second’ (affectionately known as KJ) is a 15-year-old from Johannesburg who eats, sleeps and breathes motorcycle racing.
metadata.Summary: KJ, a Grade Nine learner at Waterstone College, recalls his first “break” came in 2017 (he was 10 years old) when Neil Harran from the South African Motorcycle Racing Academy visited his school’s open day. “I was so excited to try out the demo stationary practice bike he had at the open day and everyone was very impressed with my test ride. Neil then recommended to my parents that I enrol into his academy. I was ecstatic as I knew this could be the start of great things to come,” KJ said. And it was. KJ started participating competitively in the short circuit road racing series in 2017 (he was 10 years old) in the NSF100cc Honda Cup and won a championship in 2019. In 2020, KJ claimed another title in the Clubman’s championship and finished second in the 150 cup – a category he went on to win the next year. He started competing in Italy in June 2021, in the middle of the racing season. To date, he has won multiple circuit motorcycle racing championships.
metadata.Further information: Treatment Overview Opening Scene and setup: 120 seconds I would like to start the insert with a scene of the Mononyane family, getting ready for supper. A mother is dishing up, kids around the table. Happy talking, just normal…. Voice over is explaining that this might look like an “ordinary” family. But they are far from it… We see KJ. We don’t know who he is, we are not sure what is about to happen…. We see KJ holding a spoon in his hand like a biker holds onto the throttle…. We are confused. We see a close up of KJ’s face and we crash zoom to only his eyes. Then a beautiful transition as we zoom out from a close up of his eyes at the table to a wider shot of him at the track. Pulling the helmet over his head or closing the visor…. We catch a glimpse of who he is. A bike racer. We show a few highlights with breathtaking footage of him. Quick montage. Then we cut back to him at the table. We explain that this family is driven by his mother. There are 3 members in this family. Dad is absent…. We don’t explain why yet…. Mom is supporting her talented son on the bike. We hear how much sacrifice it takes. But how talented is he really….? Motorsport SA and KJ as a person: 120 Seconds Motorsport SA’s CEO Anton Roux explains exactly how talented KJ is… It is quite astounding. He has many many wins and countless podiums on the SA circuit, and then we hear how he raced overseas! Motorsport SA supported him to be able to race in Italy. And he did well, very well, he finished in the top 10. We cut back to KJ holding a bunch of trophies, he is trying to explain which he won where, there are just too many, he forgets some of the races he won… So many podiums too. Mom is telling us what a sacrifice it has been. But she has supported him all the way. A Quick Montage of him racing and podiums, some amateur footage that the family shot, we show a very young KJ, 10 years old on a bike and we progress to today. We now understand how good he really is. Loss of his father: 120 seconds But now comes the shock. Out of the blue KJ says he gave up racing. When he lost his dad. We explain what happened to his dad. He was in a Netcare helicopter crash that took the lives of 5 emergency crews and the pilot. This happened last year in January. On a weekend when KJ was not only racing, but waited for his dad at the track. He never arrived. https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2021-02-23-netcare-911-helicopter-broke-up-in-flight-preliminary-probe-finds/ We stay with the family as they explain the trauma of going through this tragedy. KJ decided he can’t give up. It is something he and his dad started and he has to give it a good shot. His dad races with him everytime he gets on the bike. We see a sign on his race suit that says as we see a closeup of his race suit, a caption says: RIP Papa. KJ and the 2023 season and end: 120 Seconds We hear from experts that encourages KJ to go for it. To try and win National champs. We hear about the financial burden on the family. It is clearly a very expensive sport. But he has bigger ambitions. He is destined to go race in Europe in 2023, but it is simply not possible, financially. Mom speaks and gives us a bit more info of where KJ is finding himself and what the chances of racing in Europe would be. Motorsport SA is very positive, but the reality is it is tough. It leads us into his first race for 2023 at Red Star. He is only 1 of dozens, contenders, how well will he do. His first race of 2023: 120 Seconds Chaos at the race, we see lots of people running around. Fixing bikes. Loud engine noises. And in the midst of this chaos we see a very calm KJ. We pick up that pressure just doesn’t get to him. We ask him how he thinks he will do, he smiles, hopefully on the podium… Then Green light! We see the race, it's exhilarating. He comes past the camera at speed! A rush! He goes well, but it is chaotic, exciting music and action packed. We cut to the reaction of Mom, very nervous, she can’t watch! We follow him and he finishes the race. As predicted, he did very well! Details of the insert I want to approach this as a mini doccie on KJ. To showcase this talent of ours. The audience will connect to this family right from the start. It is important to make the family relatable to others. Just because he is racing motorbikes, does not make him any different to others. But what will come across is the tragedy of losing their father and husband. And their journey through this awful event. KJ will let us into his home, school, and racetrack. He will drive the narrative without coming across as arrogant. He is really down to earth and we will see a very talented, positive, driven kid. I have spent a lot of time with the family, to build up trust. So that when we have cameras, it will be normal for them.
